headline: Revenue holds steady while note refinancing dents net income
summary_short: Dropbox's Q1 2026 revenue was $629.5M, up 0.8% y/y but down 1.1% q/q, as gross margin slipped to 80% from 81% and net income fell 23.8% y/y to $114.5M on higher interest expense from a newly fully-drawn $2.0B term loan.
summary_long: Revenue grew 0.8% y/y to $629.5M on Individual-plan growth and favorable FX, offsetting the planned wind-down of FormSwift; paying users slipped to 18.09M from 18.16M y/y on the same FormSwift decision. Gross margin fell to 80% from 81% as infrastructure costs rose 9.8% on a data-center refresh. Operating income fell 6.0% y/y to $172.8M as opex outpaced the gross-profit decline. Net income dropped 23.8% y/y to $114.5M on $22.1M higher interest expense from the now-fully-drawn $2.0B term loan, which funded the $695.8M payoff of matured 2026 convertible notes. Dropbox repurchased $370M of stock in the quarter (no dividend); cash rose to $1.21B. Total ARR was $2.56B, up slightly q/q and y/y. No forward guidance was given in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Growth from Individual plans and a favorable FX impact, partly offset by the strategic decision to reduce FormSwift investment ahead of its planned 2026 wind-down.
Cost of revenue rose 9.8% on higher infrastructure costs from the data-center refresh cycle and third-party hosting fees, outpacing the 0.8% revenue gain.
Gross profit declined while R&D rose $5.8M on higher headcount and G&A rose $3.7M on a one-off prior-year tax-reserve release, partially offset by a $5.1M cut to sales & marketing.
Interest expense rose $22.1M as the term loan facility became fully drawn, and the tax provision rose $7.7M on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act impact and lower stock-comp tax benefits.
Net income fell 23.8% y/y, but the decline in diluted EPS was smaller because weighted-average diluted shares fell about 20% y/y from continued buybacks.
Tracks the same operating-income pressure — higher infrastructure and opex costs against roughly flat revenue — partially offset by the D&A add-back.
Rose $50.7M y/y mainly because the prior-year quarter included one-time cash outflows for a lease-termination fee and 2024 workforce-reduction payments that didn't recur.
Financing activities added $46.2M net, driven by $1.2B in new term-loan proceeds that funded the $695.8M payoff of maturing 2026 convertible notes and $370M of buybacks.
An $11.4 million increase in infrastructure costs, including data-center refresh equipment, facilities costs, and third-party hosting fees.
The deficit widened as $370M of share repurchases and RSU tax-withholding cash outflows exceeded the quarter's net income.

Revenue and Total ARR held roughly flat as Individual-plan growth offset the FormSwift wind-down, while refinancing the maturing 2026 notes through a fully-drawn term loan pushed net income and diluted EPS lower y/y.
